headlines.title: GD Q3 deep dive: backlog surge and segment growth set stage for sustained expansion
headlines.summary: Aerospace and defense company General Dynamics (NYSE:GD) announced better-than-expected revenue in Q3 2026, with sales up 12.9% year on year to $14.57 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $4.49 per share was 8.8% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

headlines.title: GD Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Raised Outlook and Record Backlog
headlines.summary: General Dynamics raises its 2026 earnings outlook after strong Q3 results, backed by a record $220.3B backlog, robust defense demand and Gulfstream expansion plans.

headlines.title: General Dynamics’s Q3 earnings call: our top 5 analyst questions
headlines.summary: General Dynamics delivered a quarter that exceeded Wall Street’s expectations on both revenue and profit, driven by broad-based growth across its Aerospace, Marine Systems, Combat Systems, and Technologies segments. Management credited robust order activity and steady productivity improvements—particularly in Marine Systems and Aerospace—with fueling double-digit gains in both revenue and operating earnings.

headlines.title: General Dynamics (GD) Has Investors Asking A Bigger Question
headlines.summary: General Dynamics (GD) has become a focus for investors after its third quarter 2026 earnings, reporting sales of US$14.57b and net income of US$1.23b, both higher than a year earlier. The strong third quarter update and record US$220.3b backlog have come alongside a sharp swing in sentiment, with General Dynamics delivering a 12.88% 1 month share price return and an 8.50% year to date share price gain. headlines.title: General Dynamics (GD) Stock May Be A Bargain As Raised Guidance Tests Value
headlines.summary: General Dynamics has delivered strong share price gains in recent years, and fresh contract wins and leadership changes keep the story moving. The open question for you is whether the current US$372.59 price tag is adequately backed by the cash flows the business is expected to generate. Over the past 5 years, General Dynamics has returned 105.6%, which puts a lot of long term optimism about its cash generation into the current valuation debate.

description: General Dynamics Corporation operates as an aerospace and defense company worldwide. It operates through four segments: Aerospace, Marine Systems, Combat Systems, and Technologies. The Aerospace segment produces and sells business jets; and offers aircraft maintenance and repair, management, aircraft-on-ground support, customer support and custom completion services, modifications, upgrades, and lifecycle sustainment support services. The Marine Systems segment designs and builds nuclear-powered submarines, surface combatants, and auxiliary ships for the United States Navy and Jones Act ships for commercial customers, as well as provides maintenance, modernization, and lifecycle support services for navy ships; offers and program management, planning, engineering, and design support services for submarine construction programs. The Combat Systems segment manufactures land combat solutions, such as wheeled and tracked combat vehicles, Stryker wheeled combat vehicles, piranha vehicles, weapons systems, energetics and munitions, mobile bridge systems with payloads, tactical vehicles, main battle tanks, and armored vehicles; and offers modernization programs, support and sustainment services, and development programs. The Technologies segment provides information technology solutions and mission support services; mobile communication, computers, and command-and-control mission systems; intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance solutions to military, intelligence, and federal civilian customers; cloud services, cybersecurity, network modernization, artificial intelligence; machine learning; application development, high-performance computing, and 5G and advanced communications services; and unmanned undersea vehicle manufacturing and assembly services. The company was founded in 1899 and is headquartered in Reston, Virginia.
